locations: contracts/openapi.json GET /v1/projects/{project_id}/packages (operationId listPackages): site_id is a required query parameter; no project-wide package read exists
contracts/openapi.json components.schemas.Site.package = SitePackageInfo (state const 'ready': blocked packages are visible only through history)
items.evidence: Traced: the only caller of listProjectPackages is the Overview page; it issues one listPackages per site after listSites resolves (React cache de-duplicates the page's own listSites, so no extra listSites call). Contract check: no batched or project-level package list exists; listPackages requires site_id; Site.package carries only the current ready package, but Overview needs newest-blocked-per-site and package activity, which only history has. api-fanout.json: 10-site overview: listSites done at 90 ms, listPackages 94-213 (about 120 ms of a 255 ms document, the critical path), summaries then run 216-253. Durations form a staircase (49 to 119 ms for 10 calls; 34-244 ms for 28): the API handled them close to serially, about 7 ms per site. Z-overview (28 sites): listPackages end at 378 ms but listHistoricalObservations (367 ms) ends at 398, so at 28 sites the N+1 is hidden behind that call; the '4.2-4.5 s summed API time' is the sum of parallel calls, not wall time. items.correction: The 4.2-4.5 s is not user-visible time. The N+1 is the critical path on a small project (about 47% of document time at 10 sites) and falls behind the observation list at 28; it would dominate again at 54 sites with a fast observation read. Fixing it needs a contract change (backend).
items.smallest_fix: Without any API change: start the two summaries right after getProject (they only need the timezone), and start the coverage reads in the page, so they stop waiting for the N listPackages (saves the 216-253 ms stage). Fully removing the N+1 needs one backend addition (make site_id optional on listPackages or add a project-level package list); not worth doing before a measurement on the hosted API shows Overview latency matters.

The three chunks are the module closure of lib/api/browser.ts, emitted once per page family: data (2d01), site/packages/publish/zones/qgis (3-dr7), zone draft editor (159n). items.title: Web server re-downloads and re-unzips immutable package archives on every plan view
locations: web/src/lib/api/workspace.ts:227-255 getPackageArchive/getSitePlan (React cache, per request only)
web/src/lib/sites/archive.ts:91-113 (unzipSync, JSON.parse, zod over every feature)
items.evidence: Mechanism confirmed: nothing is shared across requests. I measured the CPU part with the real lib/sites/archive.ts and lib/plan.ts (scratch harness, Fall Creek-derived synthetic layers): unzip+parse+zod+projection per getSitePlan: 41 features 3.6 ms; 401 features 17 ms; 4,001 features 116 ms; 20,001 features (the per-layer limit) 665 ms; 60,001 features 2.65 s. Cost follows feature count, not archive bytes (synthetic repeats compress to 190-540 KiB), and the Sites page runs up to six on one Node thread, so CPU adds up (6 x 116 ms = 0.7 s at 4k features each). At a real-size site (Fall Creek: 41 features, 10 KiB) a view costs a few ms. Transfer from the API to Vercel/Render was not measurable here.
items.correction: The finding frames this as transfer (multi-MB archives); the dominant cost is per-feature CPU (zod validation and projection), which a cache keyed by (packageId, archive_sha256) of the projected plan would also remove. At realistic playground-study sizes it is negligible, so it is a post-launch measurement, not a pre-launch fix. Pre-launch the added module-level cache is more code than the saved milliseconds.
items.smallest_fix: Do nothing before launch. If hosted p95 for Sites/Data shows archive time, add the in-process LRU of the projected plan keyed by (packageId, archive_sha256), consulted only after the request's own authorized read returns the sha.

items.title: Adding a Data filter has a runtime-only trap and a second parser on Reports
items.evidence: Reproduced three ways. (1) scratch filters-check.mjs copies filtersSchema verbatim from actions.ts and feeds it viewFilters output for 72 combinations of site, zones, round, observer, from, to: 0 rejected (no defect today). An extra key throws ZodError unrecognized_keys. (2) tsc in a scratch copy of the repo: adding formVersion?: string to ObservationFilters alone leaves tsc at exit 0, so the trap is real. (3) The proposed fix does not catch it: `.strict() satisfies z.ZodType<ObservationFilters>` still exits 0, because ZodType is covariant in its output and an optional key may be absent. Reports and Data do keep separate day parsers (reports/model.ts parseDayKey vs view.ts dayOrNull).
items.correction: The `satisfies z.ZodType<ObservationFilters>` fix is ineffective. A fix that works (verified: TS1360 'Property formVersion is missing', clean without it): declare the shape as an object literal `satisfies Record<keyof ObservationFilters, z.ZodType>` and build `z.object(shape).strict()`. Also latent: zod 4 z.uuid() is RFC-strict and rejects ids such as 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 that view.ts's permissive UUID regex accepts; production ids come from gen_random_uuid, so only z.guid() or a test fixture would hit it. The loadMore half is a present defect, see NEW-LOADMORE.
items.smallest_fix: Use the Record<keyof ObservationFilters, ZodType> shape guard in actions.ts. Optionally call parseView/viewFilters from the Reports page (zones and version unset) and delete its parseDayKey/dayRangeIsBackwards/conversion. Add the missing catch (NEW-LOADMORE).

items.title: Save after session expiry shows the generic crash page and loses the form (runtime confirmation of WDI-1)
items.evidence: Observed at runtime (0 API calls, boundary shown, typed input gone). Chain traced in the installed Next 16.2.7: (1) cookies cleared, so proxy.ts getClaims fails and, for a /o path, NextResponse.redirect (307, keeps method and body) is returned for the action POST. (2) The reducer's fetch(state.canonicalUrl, {method:'POST'}) uses default redirect:follow, so the browser re-POSTs the action (Next-Action header and body kept) to /sign-in?next=. (3) /sign-in's bundle does not contain the action, so action-handler.js:455-466 calls selectWorkerForForwarding and createForwardedActionResponse fetches the owning page's route pattern with redirect:'manual'; that internal request goes through the proxy unauthenticated and is 307'd again. A non-RSC answer ends in the '{}' JSON fallback (:206). (4) The client reducer (:111-121) sees no RSC content type and no x-action-redirect and throws 'An unexpected response was received from the server.'. (5) The throw happens inside start(async () => { await saveSettings(...) }) with no try/catch, so React rethrows the rejected transition at render and the nearest error boundary (project error.tsx -> ErrorView, 'Something went wrong. Your records remain available.') replaces the form. The action body never runs. Steps 3-4 are code-traced; the boundary and zero API calls were observed. The ErrorView text 'The page could not load its records' is also wrong for a failed save.
items.correction: Fix precision: catching the rejection at the call sites (the settleAction helper from WDI-1) is what stops the crash and the loss. A proxy change cannot do it alone, because any non-RSC reply, even a 401 text/plain (reducer :111-114 throws new Error(text)), still rejects. The proxy tweak (do not 307 requests carrying a next-action header) only improves the message, and per the WDI-1 check the copy must be written as a sign-in message, not reuse UNCONFIRMED_CHANGE_COPY, whose 'reload the page' advice is bad here.
items.smallest_fix: Wrap each start(async ...) action call in settleAction(promise) returning {status:'failed', message}; with a rejection, say 'Nothing was saved. You may have been signed out; sign in again in another tab, then save.' Keep the editor mounted. Optionally skip the sign-in redirect in proxy.ts for next-action requests so the typed failure path answers.

items.title: One API outage gives a shell-less 'Couldn't load this organization' on fresh load but the 'Something went wrong' boundary on client navigation

items.title: Root font-size ignored by px type tokens; 320 px at 200% root overflows and clips
items.evidence: Facts hold by code: every type-* utility sets font-size and line-height in px; body is 16px; Tailwind spacing and touch sizes are rem, so a larger root grows boxes but not text, which explains the emulated overflow at 320 px with html{font-size:200%}. Judged against WCAG: 1.4.4 Resize Text is met by browser zoom (page zoom satisfies it; text-only scaling is not required), and the layout was measured with no horizontal overflow at 320 and 390 CSS px at 100% (88 measurements), which is the 1.4.10 condition (1280 px at 400% zoom is 320 CSS px; zoom does not change root font-size). 1.4.12 spacing passed. Not re-run by me (no browser stack).
items.correction: Not a failure of 1.4.4 or 1.4.10. What is real: a user's default-font-size preference (desktop Chrome/Firefox) does nothing to text, and 'large root plus 320 px' breaks layout, a contrived combination on desktop (Android Chrome text scaling scales px text anyway; iOS Safari ignores root size). Because the token contract is shared with mobile, the change goes through the generator.
items.smallest_fix: If wanted: have the generator emit rem for web type size and line-height (px/16) and body 1rem, then re-run the 320 px at 200% root measurement and fix what still overflows.

items.title: Invite dialog never returns focus to its trigger (and 12 other dialogs the same way)
items.evidence: Library-derived and consistent with the runtime (Invite 6 of 6 trials lost focus; Edit site details, which passes trigger, returned it). Radix Dialog 1.1.23's modal content always runs event.preventDefault() in onCloseAutoFocus and then context.triggerRef.current?.focus(); triggerRef is set only by Dialog.Trigger. contour/Dialog.tsx renders a Trigger only when the trigger prop is given, so its docstring 'Focus returns to it on close' holds only then. 22 usages: 9 pass trigger; 13 are opened by an external button through open/onOpenChange (including Team and Members Invite, Data Export, all zone draft dialogs, project/org settings confirmations) and none sets onCloseAutoFocus. Focus ends on body. The command palette handles its own restore.
items.correction: Broader than 'the Invite dialog': one shared component defect affecting 13 dialogs. Severity low, not medium: no data loss, Chrome keeps a sequential-focus start point so Tab continues near the page, and WCAG 2.4.3 failure is arguable rather than certain.
items.smallest_fix: In contour/Dialog.tsx remember document.activeElement in onOpenAutoFocus (FocusScope reads it before moving focus) and in onCloseAutoFocus call event.preventDefault() and focus it if still connected (composeEventHandlers skips Radix's own handler when defaultPrevented). About 8 lines fix all 13.

The behaviour is real: the layout's redirect(collectPath) for collectOnly runs in parallel with the page (Next renders layouts and pages concurrently), and only the overview, reports and qgis pages repeat the collectOnly check; forms, forms/versions, sites, data and others do not, so their reads run and their output is discarded. Authorization (the question asked): listForms is allowed to any project member by design. The route is user_transaction with the caller's id, and RLS gives members published and retired versions only (policy member_reads_published_versions, project member) while drafts are manager-only (manager_reads_drafts). items.title: Zone editor save status says 'Checking whether your last change was saved...' while nothing is checking (indefinitely in an outage) and a fast-failing PUT loops without backoff
locations: web/src/features/zones/editor/save-queue.ts:386-387 (status text), get-ok verify branch and get-failed branch (:236-262, :296-306)
items.evidence: Reproduced at reducer level with the real save-queue.ts (scratch repro/j6.mjs). Case A (API down, browser online): put-failed(network) issues a verify GET; get-failed(network) leaves reading:null, inFlight set, pause 'unconfirmed' and returns no command, yet saveStatus still returns 'Checking whether your last change was saved…' because the text derives from pause only. Nothing schedules a retry: the hook re-flushes only on an edit debounce, blur, pagehide, visibilitychange, the online event or the 429 timer. So the line stays until the manager edits or switches tab, not for 6 s as the runtime waited. Case B (only the PUT fails fast, the GET works): get-ok at the same revision calls trySend again; 1000 PUT/GET pairs in a row with no delay, cap or backoff (matches the emulated 40 s aborted PUT, which would loop at network speed). The pause behaviour is pinned by the unit test 'a failed read keeps checking'. Leave guard and disabled publish stay on, so no data is lost.
items.correction: Real trigger for case B needs a PUT that fails quickly while GET works (path-specific proxy, WAF, CORS) or 15 s PUT timeouts (one pair per 15-30 s, benign), so impact is low. The runtime's '6 s' understated case A.
items.smallest_fix: (1) When pause is 'unconfirmed' and reading is null, show 'Not saved yet · DECA Mark could not be reached. Your changes are kept in this tab.' (2) Add one backoff timer in useDraftSaving (for example 5, 10, 20, 30 s) that flushes while the pause still needs a read, and apply the same backoff before the resend after a verify that found 'not saved'.

items.title: fm-place cookie survives sign-out; sb auth cookie is JS-readable with ~400-day expiry
items.evidence: Code-derived plus installed library. (a) fm-place: signOut deletes only fm-verify-email, fm-recovery-* and fm-email-sent, so the path-only cookie (1 year) survives. It is read only by /o and passed through homeFor, which requires the SAFE_PATH regex and that the current person's own index contains that org or project, else it is ignored. Another account lands there only if it is already a member of that project, so nothing leaks. The real cross-account carry-over is the palette recents in localStorage (WDI-5). (b) @supabase/ssr 0.12.7 defaults are httpOnly:false and maxAge 400 days. JS-readability is required here: the browser calls createBrowserClient().auth.getSession() and sends the bearer token to the API directly (package upload up to 24 MiB, zone draft autosave, exports). The cookie lifetime is not session validity, which Supabase enforces server-side (jwt_expiry 3600, refresh rotation on; timebox and inactivity limits are commented out in local config and are a hosted-plan setting).
items.correction: (a) is benign by construction; an optional one-line store.delete('fm-place') in signOut. (b) is refuted as a finding: standard library defaults on a design that needs them. The only related point is that no CSP is configured (see NEW-headers).
items.smallest_fix: None required. Optional: delete fm-place in signOut.

items.title: Org no-access pages lack an h1; sign-in gives no signed-out reason; signed-in users can open /sign-in

items.title: Multi-word search matches any word
items.evidence: Reproduced with the real searchLoaded (scratch repro/j10.mjs). The search splits on whitespace and requires every term to be a substring of the record's search text (terms.every(...)): AND, not any-word. 'synthetic nope' returns no rows, which any-word semantics would not. The unit test pins this ('garden sandpit' returns the one record with both, 'no such words' returns none). The runtime result ('record 7' kept all 8 rows) is a seed artifact: every seeded row's label is OBS-700000 (the runtime's own note), and the search text includes the label, so '7' is a substring of every row and 'record' is in every answer.
items.correction: Not a defect. The only real property is substring (not word-boundary) matching, so short numeric terms match ids, labels and dates, which is normal for this kind of box.
items.smallest_fix: None.

items.title: Rotating the device remounts the field map and the step panel
items.evidence: Reproduced at reconciler level, not on a device. scratchpad w2/mobile/repro/rotate.cjs uses the real react 19.2.3 and react-test-renderer with a skeleton that has the same element types and positions as the return tree. Portrait to landscape logs: unmount status, unmount panel content, unmount CollectMap, mount CollectMap, mount status, mount panel content. The reverse switch gives the same. Cause in code: landscape is body>[View>[View(mapSlot)>CollectMap, View(status)], KAV]; portrait is body>[View(mapSlot)>CollectMap, View|null, KAV]. The first View pairs with the first View, then CollectMap meets a View and remounts. The KAV sits at index 1 in one tree and 2 in the other, so the panel remounts. The camera restarts at placed ?? zone.centre (CollectMap.tsx:550-556). The aim store lives in CollectScreen and survives, so it can be stale until the new map reports a region (not device-verified). CollectMap's hidden/filter/selected state resets, and so do useMyLocation's mount and unmount watchers. ReviewStep's saving flag is local state, but session.save() is one local SQLite transaction (observation-actions.ts:156-205), so the double-save window is milliseconds. A second save would fail on the primary key with 'Could not save'. app.config orientation is 'default', so auto-rotate is on.
items.correction: None to the claim. The double-save consequence is negligible and should not carry weight. The camera and map-state loss is the real cost. The CollectScreen.tsx:64-70 doc comment ('MapLibre stays mounted') is untrue across rotation.
items.smallest_fix: Render one tree with identical wrapper Views and switch flexDirection and sizes through style only. Put map, status and panel at fixed child positions, so a null status takes a slot rather than shifting siblings. Keep the 46% slot and the instant height change.

items.title: Bottom tab bar absent from the XCUITest accessibility tree on project screens
items.evidence: Code only. The dock is a custom tabBar rendered by expo-router's bottom-tabs fork as a sibling after the screens container. Its container is a plain View with accessibilityRole 'tablist' inside an absolute, pointerEvents='box-none' anchor, with three Pressables (accessible by default) carrying role 'tab', a baked label '<name>, tab, i of 3' and selected state. I found nothing in the navigator wrapper or the dock that hides it from accessibility (no accessibilityElementsHidden or importantForAccessibility in bottom-tabs). On iOS RN maps both 'tab' and 'tablist' to UIAccessibilityTraitNone (RCTViewManager.m:105-108; only role 'tabbar' gets the TabBar trait), so VoiceOver has no native tab-bar semantics, and the position text is baked into the label. On Android, role TAB sets roleDescription 'tab' (ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:704) so the baked ', tab,' may be spoken twice (unverified). Why the XCUITest list omitted the dock cannot be derived from source. Candidates are the tool's element filtering and the box-none anchor. Needs an Accessibility Inspector or WDA tree dump on a simulator. The dock is visible in the screenshots.
items.correction: Absence from the tree is an observation I cannot confirm or explain from code; it is not shown to be a VoiceOver defect.
items.smallest_fix: Dump the tree with Accessibility Inspector on the project screen. If the tabs are absent, test removing accessibilityRole 'tablist' from the container and setting accessible={false} on the anchor. Otherwise no change.

items.title: expo-linking warns that app.config.ts declares three URI schemes and ignores two

Ignoring: decamark, fieldmaps, com.fieldmaps.collector.dev'). resolveScheme warns whenever the config has more than one scheme (extraSchemes.length); the native bundle id is always appended to the message but never triggers it on its own. Nothing generates fieldmaps:// links. Only 'fieldmaps' is rename-era, and it is the S5 item.

items.title: Training practice records can never upload; Account, Sign out, Saved and the guide describe them as held for the project
items.evidence: Code only; not seen in the native run. Account and Observations also name the same states differently (pending = 'On device' vs 'Held'; local-only = 'Held' vs 'On device only').

When isShellObservation, say 'Practice record: stays on this device and is never uploaded' in SavedStep, the guide and leaving.ts, and exclude practice records from the sign-out 'not been uploaded' count. Use one state mapping on Account and Observations.

## (1) Forms list, versions, detail, editor
Reproduced:
- Create draft: Versions, then Start new draft, opened workspace-check-v5 (a copy of v4).
- Change a question label, Save draft: the toast 'Draft saved' appeared. After a reload the edit was kept.
- Publish: the Publish page shows the change review ('1 question changed'). It also says 'Using another version of this form now: Fall Creek test site.' and 'Go to Sites to prepare a map package'. After the checkbox and Publish, v5 was published.

What the pages say about versions and sites:
- The draft editor says only 'Nothing reaches observers until you publish it'. It says nothing about which version observers collect with or which sites use which version.
- Its collector preview header reads 'Fall Creek test site ... MAP v13 workspace-check-v5 draft', although Fall Creek's current package binds v1.
- The Forms list gives no per-site version.
- The Versions list is correct per version: v5, v4 and v3 'No site', v1 'Fall Creek test site'.
- The Site page is correct: 'Form version workspace-check-v1'.

### UXW-2: confirmed, severity medium kept
Run in the clean project, uxw2-clean:

The prior corrections stand: the Publish page and the Site and Versions pages do tell the truth, and the gap is the Forms row and the Overview.

## (2) WDI-1 / J-1: reproduced at 1440, with unsaved label edit then Save draft
- **cookie-clear** (`ctx.clearCookies()`):
  - The action POST gets a 307, then POST /sign-in returns 200, then the console shows 'An unexpected response was received from the server.'
  - The project error boundary renders: 'REQUEST INTERRUPTED / Something went wrong. Your records remain available.'
  - The editor is unmounted and the edit is gone. 'Try again' leads to the sign-in redirect.
  - This is the session-ended chain that was only code-traced before. It is now run.
- **aborted action POST** (`route.abort`): 'TypeError: Failed to fetch', then the same error boundary. The editor unmounts. Try again remounts the editor with the previously saved wording; the edit is lost. No beforeunload dialog appears.
- **offline** (`setOffline`, the finding's own scenario): same boundary. Try again cannot recover.
- 390 spot-check of the aborted POST: identical.

The boundary page says 'What failed: The page could not load its records'. That is false here: the page had loaded and the save failed. There is no 'Nothing was saved' copy and no hint that the edits were lost.

Other Forms actions, aborted POST (j3): Start new draft, Publish, Retire, Discard and 'Start a new draft from this version' all reach the same boundary. The dialog is gone and there is no inline 'Nothing was X.' note. Only the editor loses unsaved data, but all five give a wrong message and an unclear outcome.

Verdict: the finding holds for the three cases I ran. The prior check's severity of medium is reasonable. Its correction on the fix copy stands, since a bare proxy tweak would produce the generic UNCONFIRMED copy rather than a sign-in message.

Smaller new note (low, DESIGN PREFERENCE): ErrorView's 'Reference REQ-939D-68' was identical across runs and viewports. ErrorView.tsx:17-28 says a client error has no digest, so a hash of its message stands in. It cannot be matched to a server log, although the card says 'send the reference to your organization owner'.
